periods.analysis: Enrollment opened this series at 537 students, comfortably above the 400-student target and green. That number reflects a strong summer push through the Main Library, East Harbor Branch, and the mobile library stop at Bayside Courts, where staff paired reading logs with meal-site outreach. I see this as more than a participation count: it is 537 children keeping reading habits alive while school is out. The operational story is that the June-to-August schedule, school flyers, and recreation-center referrals worked together for families.
periods.recommendations: Sustain the green result by keeping the library-recreation joint registration table at all major summer camp check-ins next year. Extend the approach by adding a standing enrollment script for mobile library staff on the South Route and Airport Corridor Route. Before the next cycle, compare attendance-to-enrollment by site so we can protect the locations that are turning sign-ups into completed literacy hours.

periods.analysis: Enrollment was 455 students, down 82 from 537, but still safely green against the 400-student target. The quarter-over-quarter dip is expected after the summer peak, and staff kept the floor strong by converting summer participants into fall reading clubs at Northgate, Central, and Seaport branches. For residents, the important point is that the program did not disappear when school resumed; it became a steadier after-school support. The Homework Harbor cohort at East Harbor also helped retain families who first came through summer meal-site outreach.
periods.recommendations: Sustain fall enrollment by continuing direct handoffs from summer literacy coaches to branch-based after-school leads. Extend the strongest conversion practice by sending targeted texts to families who enrolled in Q3 but did not attend a Q4 session. Watch the school-calendar pinch points around November conferences and winter break, and pre-schedule make-up reading circles so families do not lose momentum.

periods.analysis: Enrollment rose to 471 students, up 16 from 455, and remained green. That modest gain tells me the winter re-engagement work was effective, especially the New Year Reading Reset at Central Library and the Saturday family sessions at Westport Recreation Center. Families are making room for literacy even during a busy school quarter, which is exactly the resident outcome we want. Staff also used chronic-absenteeism referral lists from partner schools carefully, offering library-based support without making families feel labeled.
periods.recommendations: Sustain the Q1 lift by keeping Saturday family literacy blocks at Westport and East Harbor through spring registration. Extend the school partnership by asking each participating elementary school to identify one attendance-support liaison for literacy referrals. Use the Q1 cohort list to invite students early into the Q2 summer enrollment window, with priority outreach to families who attended at least two winter sessions.

periods.analysis: Enrollment increased sharply to 562 students, up 91 from 471, the strongest result in this arc and well above target. This is what good preparation looks like: April school visits, bilingual registration at the Harborview Family Resource Fair, and bundled sign-ups through recreation camps all fed the same pipeline. For children and caregivers, the benefit is simple and powerful: summer learning was easy to find, easy to join, and connected to places they already trust. The libraries team also coordinated with Parks on the Bayfront, Southside, and Glen Marina camp rosters so literacy time followed students instead of asking every family to make a separate trip.
periods.recommendations: Sustain this green result by locking in the April school-visit calendar before spring break each year. Extend the camp-linked model to two additional recreation sites, starting with Riverview Gym and Harbor Heights Field House. Preserve service quality by checking tutor-to-student ratios weekly in June, because a high enrollment number only matters if children still receive attentive reading support.

periods.analysis: Enrollment was 535 students, down 27 from 562, and still solidly green. After the very strong Q2 build, this small seasonal easing is manageable and keeps us well above the 400-student target. I am pleased that the decline did not erase access gains in the Airport Corridor and Bayside neighborhoods, where pop-up registration at Route 12 bus stops and the Maritime Museum family night continued to bring in students. The resident outcome remains strong: more than five hundred young readers stayed connected through the heart of summer.
periods.recommendations: Sustain the summer reach by repeating the Route 12 and Maritime Museum pop-up enrollment model next year. Extend retention work by flagging students who registered in Q2 but did not attend by mid-July, then assigning branch staff to make warm reminder calls. Keep a close operating eye on late-summer staffing coverage, especially at Southside and East Harbor, so vacations do not reduce session capacity.

periods.analysis: Enrollment was 450 students, down 85 from 535, while remaining green. The larger post-summer step-down mirrors the prior year’s Q4 pattern, but the floor is still 50 students above target, which matters for continuity. Staff protected access by moving popular summer readers into the Fall Pages program and by using school open-house tables at Lincoln, Chavez, and Harborview STEM Academy. From a family perspective, the program stayed visible after summer ended, even as sports, homework, and holiday schedules competed for time.
periods.recommendations: Sustain the green floor by making Fall Pages the default continuation offer for every Q3 participant. Extend outreach to caregivers by sending a one-page branch calendar home through school open-house packets and aftercare providers. For the next Q4, test one weekday early-evening family session at Central and one at East Harbor to reduce conflicts with after-school transportation.

periods.analysis: Enrollment rebounded to 471 students, up 21 from 450, returning to the same level reached in 2025-Q1 and staying green. That repeatable winter performance is a good sign: the program is no longer relying only on summer excitement to meet the target. The strongest operational contributor was the Read Into Spring campaign, with library cards issued on-site at three recreation centers and a simple QR registration path for caregivers. For residents, this means literacy support is becoming a year-round habit, not a one-season service.
periods.recommendations: Sustain the year-round pattern by keeping Read Into Spring as the standard Q1 campaign name and schedule. Extend the QR registration path to printed utility-bill inserts and clinic waiting-room flyers, using the same short form families already recognize. Review which Q1 sites produced repeat attendance, not just enrollment, and shift one outreach shift from any low-conversion site to the highest-performing branch.

periods.analysis: Enrollment climbed to 558 students, up 87 from 471, again delivering a strong green result just below last year’s Q2 peak of 562. The two-year arc is encouraging: Harborview is repeatedly building a large summer literacy cohort before school lets out. Staff executed the familiar playbook well, with early school visits, camp roster matching, and bilingual sign-up support at the Seaport Community Day and Airport Families Resource Night. The resident outcome is clear: 558 students entered summer with a reading connection already in place.
periods.recommendations: Sustain the Q2 enrollment engine by finalizing school-visit dates, camp roster imports, and bilingual staffing assignments by March 15 each year. Extend the model by adding a small teen reading-mentor cohort at Central and Southside to support the larger student volume without diluting attention. Because the result is green, use the next quarter to focus on completion and engagement metrics, making sure these 558 enrollments translate into regular reading sessions and confident students.

periods.analysis: September enrollment reached 570, above the 400 target and up from June’s recorded 558. Enrollment is open, but the separate summer-session launch milestone remains in progress; sign-ups should not be presented as completed sessions.
periods.recommendations: Check attendance and instructor coverage at the six neighborhood locations before closing the summer-session launch milestone.
